description: evmonly-loadtest: where a block's serial time goes, and which stage of the pipeline is the constraint.

panels.description: Transactions finished per second, the headline number for a run.
panels.title: Transactions / Second

panels.description: Blocks finished per second.
panels.title: Blocks / Second

panels.description: Where the executor's main loop spends the clock: blocked on upstream, executing, or writing state. Wall time of the single executor goroutine, so the slices sum to elapsed time. Block generation and signature verification run on other goroutines and appear here only as the stall they cause, 'waiting for upstream'; the Pipeline Stages row shows what that work costs.
panels.title: Main Loop Wall Time — by Stage

panels.description: The same three stages over time, as milliseconds of wall clock per block. Wall time of the single executor goroutine, so the slices sum to elapsed time. Block generation and signature verification run on other goroutines and appear here only as the stall they cause, 'waiting for upstream'; the Pipeline Stages row shows what that work costs.
panels.title: Main Loop Time Per Block — by Stage

panels.description: The stages above broken into their phases. Same total, so the shares refine the stages one level down. Wall time of the single executor goroutine, so the slices sum to elapsed time. Block generation and signature verification run on other goroutines and appear here only as the stall they cause, 'waiting for upstream'; the Pipeline Stages row shows what that work costs.
panels.title: Main Loop Wall Time — by Phase

panels.description: Each phase over time, as milliseconds of wall clock per block. Wall time of the single executor goroutine, so the slices sum to elapsed time. Block generation and signature verification run on other goroutines and appear here only as the stall they cause, 'waiting for upstream'; the Pipeline Stages row shows what that work costs.
panels.title: Main Loop Time Per Block — by Phase
Pipeline Stages (concurrent work, not wall time)

panels.description: Share of upstream work between building blocks and recovering senders. Block generation and signature verification each run across many goroutines, so this is total work across those workers, not wall time. It is what the main loop's 'waiting for upstream' is waiting on.
panels.title: Upstream Stages — Work Share

panels.description: Upstream work per block, summed across that stage's goroutines. Block generation and signature verification each run across many goroutines, so this is total work across those workers, not wall time. It is what the main loop's 'waiting for upstream' is waiting on.
panels.title: Upstream Stages — Worker-ms Per Block
Throughput
panels.description: Transactions and blocks finished per second.

Storage cost left on the critical path. The commit runs behind the next block, so the block pays the handoff (commit_state) plus whatever the previous commit had not finished (await_commit) — not the write itself. await_commit near zero means the overlap is working.
panels.title: Commit Pipelining — Blocked vs Handoff

panels.description: Execution split into its OCC stages. occ_speculate is parallel across executor workers; occ_merge is serial, so it does not shrink with more workers.
panels.title: Execute — OCC Stages Per Block

panels.description: Encoding and view setup per block.
panels.title: Encode and View Per Block
Blocks / Second by Stage
panels.description: Input, prepared and finished. Preparation running ahead of finishing means the executor is the constraint; the two converging means preparation is.

panels.title: Queued Blocks
panels.description: Prepared blocks waiting for the executor. Pinned at queue-size means the executor is behind; near zero means it is starved. Built ahead counts streaming blocks held behind a slower height; pinned near twice --builders means one builder is holding the rest back.

panels.title: OCC
panels.description: Attempts, fallbacks and reruns per second. A fallback drops the block to sequential execution, so a nonzero rate here caps throughput regardless of executor-workers.

panels.title: View Cache Hit Rate
panels.description: Hits over lookups per cache. Execution reads accounts and code through this cache, and a miss is handed to a shared reader pool and waited on, so the miss rate sets execution cost.

panels.title: View Cache Misses / Second
panels.description: Misses per second per cache. Each one costs a hand-off to the reader pool and a blocking wait.

panels.title: Cache Miss Latency (p99)
panels.description: How long a miss takes to resolve, which is the reader-pool round trip rather than the disk read.

panels.title: View Phase Time Per Block
panels.description: Seconds per block inside the view manager, by phase and cache.

panels.title: View Cache Size
panels.description: Resident bytes and entries per cache, against the configured budget.

panels.title: State Commit Phases Per Block
panels.description: Seconds per block inside the giga state commit, which is the commit_state stage above.

panels.title: Receipt Store Write Phases Per Block
panels.description: Seconds per block inside the receipt store write.

panels.title: Go Heap
panels.description: Heap in use and next GC target.

panels.title: GC
panels.description: Garbage collections per second and the fraction of CPU they take.

panels.title: Goroutines and CPU
panels.description: Goroutine count and process CPU seconds per second; the latter against core count shows how much of the machine the run uses.
